policy: Traits are scoped to a work and person. Reviewed physical details are paraphrases of the linked primary edition. Remaining appearance, skin shades and costumes are artistic choices, not measurements or ethnic identities claimed by the author. Dramatic insults and metaphor do not establish biological facts.

The creature.description: About eight feet tall, proportionately large; yellow skin, flowing lustrous black hair, watery eyes and black lips. No green skin, flat skull, neck bolts or forehead stitching.

Elizabeth Bennet.description: Expressive dark eyes and a light, pleasing figure. Hair colour and exact height are artistic choices.
anchors: beautiful expression of her dark eyes

Mr. Darcy.description: Tall, handsome and dignified. No numeric height is supplied in this description.

Rochester.description: Broad dark eyebrows, black hair across a square forehead, strong features and an olive complexion; mature, rugged rather than a conventionally handsome young romantic lead. Later injury changes his sight and hand.

Jane Eyre.description: Small, plain young woman, not a statuesque glamour model; child in the school episodes and adult in the governess episodes. Dress is restrained and practical. Eye and hair colours here are artistic choices.

Dorian Gray.description: Handsome young man with crisp golden hair, blue eyes and scarlet lips. He stays youthful while the painted portrait deteriorates.

Count Dracula.description: At the castle introduction, a tall old man dressed all in black with a long white moustache, a strongly aquiline nose and heavy eyebrows. His appearance becomes younger later; do not hold the old moustache fixed through every scene.

Long John Silver.description: Very tall and strong, broad pale smiling face. Left leg amputated near the hip; a crutch under his left shoulder. Do not replace this with a wooden peg leg.
anchors: His left leg was cut off close by the hip

Griffin.description: When concealed, white facial bandages, blue glasses, gloves and dark-brown velvet jacket. Before invisibility, about six feet tall and broad, nearly albino with a pink-and-white face and red eyes. When undressed after transformation, body genuinely invisible, not a translucent visible ghost.
anchors: pink and white face and red eyes

Bluntschli.description: A Swiss professional soldier aged thirty-four, with blue eyes and practical, energetic bearing. Clothes are dishevelled on his flight into Raina's room.

Raina.description: Bulgarian woman aged twenty-three, rather than the seventeen-year-old Bluntschli assumes.

Eliza.description: Around eighteen to twenty, initially in a dusty black straw sailor hat with unwashed mousy hair and worn clothing; later clean, elegantly dressed, visibly the same person. Class changes her dress and manner, not her skin colour.

Higgins.description: Robust, energetic man of about forty, in a professional black frock coat, white collar and black silk tie.

Pickwick.description: Bald head and circular spectacles; keep these recognisable throughout his travels.

Philip Carey.description: Begins as a nine-year-old orphan and grows into an adult. Has a club foot; portray disability naturally, without adding a missing leg or using deformity as a marker of villainy.

Kim.description: Child of Irish parents growing up in India, with deeply sun-darkened skin. Do not confuse ancestry with a fixed pale complexion or change his skin when he enters a British school.

The lama.description: An elderly Tibetan Buddhist lama and pilgrim. Tibetan, not a Hindu priest; keep Buddhist robes and pilgrimage materials coherent.

Margaret Hale.description: Tall and finely made, with dark hair. Starts as a young woman of eighteen, often wearing restrained Victorian clothing.

Maggie Tulliver.description: Long black hair, dark eyes and a brown complexion. Her English family contrasts her appearance with their fairer relatives; do not invent a different ethnicity from that contrast. Ages from a child into a young woman.

Adam.description: Muscular, large-boned carpenter nearly six feet tall, straight jet-black hair and dark eyes; practical working clothes with sleeves rolled up.

Athena.description: Grey-eyed goddess; disguises herself as a human adviser in some episodes. Divine identity does not require wings.

Odysseus.description: Athena gives him deep curling locks in scenes of restored splendour. Other scenes require a battered traveller or an aged beggar disguise, rather than permanent kingly armour.

Gregor.description: After the opening transformation, a large brown, segmented vermin with armour-like back and many thin legs. Exact zoological species is unspecified; do not assert that Kafka defines him as a cockroach.

Hermia.description: Noticeably shorter than Helena; their height contrast matters to their quarrel. Exact measurements are not given.

Helena.description: Taller than Hermia, who calls her a maypole during their quarrel.

The Queen.description: About forty-three in the present dream: inherited the throne at thirteen thirty years earlier. A mature ruler supporting scientific education; complexion, hair, sari colour and royal costume are artistic interpretations.

Othello.description: A Black Moor and experienced general serving Venice, older than his young wife. Specific modern ancestry and numerical height are not stated by the play. Dignified human depiction, not the animal caricatures used by his enemies.

Heathcliff.description: Dark complexion; his childhood origins are uncertain. Lockwood compares his appearance using a racialised period label, which does not prove an ethnic identity. Child in the early recollection, powerful gentleman later.

Cathy Linton.description: The younger Cathy has dark Earnshaw eyes, fair skin, small features and yellow curling hair; distinguish her from her mother Catherine Earnshaw.

Magwitch.description: In the opening marsh encounter, coarse grey clothing, an iron on his leg, broken shoes and a rag around his head. Later appearance and clothes change.
anchors: fearful man, all in coarse grey

Miss Havisham.description: White hair and an aged, faded bridal outfit with veil and bridal flowers. The dress has yellowed; it is not a pristine new wedding gown.

Fagin.description: An older man with matted red hair, initially in a worn flannel gown. Avoid exaggerating Jewish identity into a caricature of facial anatomy.

Bill Sikes.description: Stoutly built, about thirty-five, wearing a black velveteen coat, soiled drab breeches and lace-up half boots.

Harriet Smith.description: Short, plump and fair, with blue eyes and light hair. Distinct from Emma and the taller elegant Jane Fairfax.

Jane Fairfax.description: Elegant and graceful, of medium build and a height usually considered tall but not very tall; initially somewhat delicate in health.

Catherine Morland.description: Seventeen during the Bath journey. Childhood description has a thin awkward figure, sallow complexion and dark lank hair; by her teens her figure and complexion have improved. Do not freeze the childhood description over the adult scenes.

Mary Crawford.description: Lively dark eyes and a clear brown complexion; Austen contrasts her appearance with tall, fair, fuller figures without implying a different nationality.
anchors: lively dark eye, clear brown complexion

Belinda.description: Two curling locks hanging behind her neck and a sparkling cross at her breast, in an elaborate early eighteenth-century gown. One lock is cut; do not depict her as losing all her hair.

Lucie Manette.description: Short, slight young woman with golden hair and blue eyes.
anchors: a quantity of golden hair, a pair of blue eyes

Elizabeth-Jane.description: Light-brown hair; the contrast with the expected black hair is part of Henchard’s uncertainty over her identity.

Silas Marner.description: Large brown eyes, initially short-sighted, and increasingly bent shoulders; white hair in the later scenes after sixteen years have passed.

Eppie.description: Golden-haired child who grows into a young woman over the narrative; keep her recognisable while changing age appropriately.
anchors: hair looked like the dash of gold

The Eloi.description: Small, slight future humans, with one first seen about four feet high in a purple tunic and belt. They are not miniature fairies with wings.

The Morlocks.description: Pale, chinless faces and large lidless pinkish-grey eyes; subterranean future humans, not pig-headed monsters.

The Mariner.description: Old sailor with a long grey beard and striking, glittering eyes when he stops the Wedding Guest.
anchors: long grey beard and glittering eye

Della.description: Initially brown hair falling below her knees. After selling it, small close curls; this change must carry through the remaining cards.

Baloo.description: Large old brown bear, depicted as an animal with brown fur.

Bagheera.description: Black panther, inky black with markings visible in some light; feline anatomy, not a person in a black costume.
anchors: Bagheera the Black Panther, inky black all over

Shere Khan.description: Tiger with a lame paw, natural feline anatomy and stripes.

Kaa.description: Rock python, about thirty feet long, blunt-nosed head and a newly shed patterned skin; not a green cartoon cobra.

Rikki-tikki-tavi.description: Small mongoose with a weasel-like head, fur and tail, pink eyes and a restless pink nose; not a cat.
anchors: His eyes and the end of his restless nose were pink

Kotick.description: The white seal, with seal anatomy; distinct from the brown bears and forest mammals of the separate Mowgli stories.

The Martians.description: Large rounded grey leathery bodies or heads roughly four feet across, dark eyes and tentacles. The walking tripod is their machine, not the shape of their body.

Mathilde.description: Initially a young woman dressed exquisitely for the ball. After ten years of labour, older-looking with disordered hair, worn skirts and reddened working hands; keep the same underlying face.
anchors: frowsy hair, skirts askew and red hands

Richard.description: The play portrays a disabled king with an impaired gait and physical asymmetry. Portray disability respectfully; costume and actions communicate ambition without making disability itself a sign of evil.

The fairy lady.description: Long hair, light-footed movement and wild eyes; hair and eye colours are not specified in these lines.
anchors: Her hair was long, her foot was light

Mephistopheles.description: After the first summoning, returns disguised as an old Franciscan friar, as Faustus requests. Use an elderly human appearance and Franciscan habit through their conversations; the initial frightening form is not the continuing disguise.
anchors: Go, and return an old Franciscan friar
Re-enter MEPHISTOPHILIS like a Franciscan friar

Duessa.description: At her deceptive introduction, a richly dressed lady in scarlet red embroidered with gold, wearing a Persian-style crown. Her attractive disguise later gives way to revealed ugliness; retain the distinction from Una.
anchors: A goodly lady clad in scarlet red

Becky Sharp.description: Small, slight, pale, sandy-haired and green-eyed. Preserve sandy blonde hair rather than dark hair throughout her social rise.

Amelia Sedley.description: Brown hair and large eyes; her face becomes white and thin during her grief after George dies. Her hair is not blonde.
anchors: Her face was white and thin

William Dobbin.description: Very tall and ungainly, large hands, feet and ears; closely cropped black hair at his early appearance, later greying.
anchors: closely cropped head of black hair

Rawdon Crawley.description: A very large young dandy, six feet tall, with a loud voice. Maintain his broad size and distinguish him from tall ungainly Dobbin.

The Knight.description: Plain coarse fustian tunic stained by mail; modest travelling clothes, rather than a bright white crusader tabard.

The Miller.description: Broad, muscular and large-framed, broad red beard, white coat and blue hood.

The Wife of Bath.description: Broad hips, fair ruddy face, separated teeth, fine kerchiefs, scarlet stockings; broad hat over a wimple when riding.

The Pardoner.description: Thin shoulder-length wax-yellow hair, smooth beardless face, glaring eyes; medieval cap with a Veronica badge, without an enveloping hood.

Harry Bailly.description: Large man with prominent eyes; keep his welcoming innkeeper role distinct from the pilgrims.

Marlow.description: Sunken cheeks, yellowish complexion, straight back and a thin ascetic appearance at the Thames framing scene; preserve a thoughtful storyteller rather than a robust action-hero build.

Kurtz.description: Conspicuously bald, exceptionally tall-looking and severely wasted, with visible thin limbs during his final illness. His reported apparent seven-foot length is an impression, not an exact measured height.

Friday.description: Long straight black hair, a tawny or olive-brown complexion, round face and lively eyes. Do not replace the described straight hair with tightly curled hair or infer a modern racial identity from period comparisons.
anchors: His hair was long and black
His face was round and plump

Crusoe.description: Visibly age through the island years: his stay lasts more than twenty-eight years. In his later island appearance he keeps a short beard with conspicuously long moustaches; island clothing is improvised, including goat-skin garments.

Sophia Western.description: A young woman in her eighteenth year, somewhat tall, delicate and proportionate. Black hair, formerly reaching her waist, is cut and curled around her neck; full arched eyebrows.

Moll.description: Her appearance must age through her life. At transportation she is in her sixty-first year, and by the final return to England she is nearly seventy; the late thief, prisoner and memoir narrator are not a twenty-year-old bride.

The Lancashire husband.description: Aging partner: at their late return he is sixty-eight. Keep his recognizable earlier face while visibly aging him for the later prison, transportation and prosperity scenes.

Apollyon.description: A composite allegorical monster with fish-like scales, dragon wings, bear-like feet, a lion-like mouth and fire and smoke from the belly. Do not substitute a generic human knight with horns.

Cyril Fielding.description: Already over forty when he comes to India; portray a mature civilian schoolmaster, distinct from younger officials and Dr Aziz. Hair and eye colours are artistic choices.

Ronny Heaslop.description: A civilian city magistrate, not an army officer. Use period civilian official clothing; gold military medals and a military uniform are not supported by his role. Additional physical attributes are artistic choices.
